text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes develops slowly over years, and early symptoms are often mild or go completely unnoticed.

Many people have no symptoms at all during the early stages and only discover they have the condition during routine blood work or after complications arise. If you are over age 45 or have risk factors like overweight, physical inactivity, or a family history, consult a doctor for a simple blood test (such as an A1C or fasting blood glucose) as detailed by the Mayo Clinic.
